title: Priv-VPC IAM binding sequencer and policy hardening playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) customers need a repeatable Terraform module and operational playbook to provision least-privilege IAM/RBAC for Redwood Private while supporting safe upgrades, drift detection, and health checks across accounts and regions. Existing artifacts are inconsistent across repos and several customers experienced outages during a policy rollout in 2025.

Goal: Deliver a single terraform module + CI workflow + runbook that: generates minimal role/binding state for services and operators, exposes a deterministic binding sequencing mechanism for zero-downgrade windows, includes state migration hooks for breaking changes, and wires in continuous drift detection and runtime health checks.

Scope: module code, CI pipelines (plan/apply gating), upgrade playbook (sequencing + canary rollout), monitoring dashboards, and acceptance tests. Not in scope: deep per-customer custom policy authoring — those remain in customer overlays.

Why this matters: private deployments demand both strict least-privilege posture and high reliability; unsafe policy churn breaks control-plane operations and customer workloads. This work reduces manual toil for SREs and Solutions Engineers while enabling faster, safer upgrades for Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module (module/priv_iam) produces deterministic minimal RBAC IAM bindings for core Redwood services and operator personas
Module exports a binding sequencing plan (ordered apply manifest) and an idempotent migration hook API for breaking changes
CI pipeline validates plan differences and blocks apply when the plan contains high-risk destructive changes unless explicitly approved by a security reviewer
Automated drift detection runs daily and opens alerts in PagerDuty/console when service-account role attachments deviate from module state
Runbook with explicit canary rollout steps, rollback procedure, and post-upgrade validation checklist is published and reviewed by SRE and Security
End-to-end tests exercise create -> upgrade -> rollback across at least two cloud accounts and one on-prem target using ephemeral infra and assert no customer-facing downtime
tasks: Design module interface: inputs (service_map, operator_principals, environment_tags), outputs (binding_sequence, migration_hooks) and explicit ordering metadata
Implement Terraform module with option to emit a 'delta-sequence' file that lists APPLIES in safe order
Create migration hook spec and example hooks for renaming roles and splitting large bindings into narrower ones
Add CI plan gating: terraform plan diff scan for destructive ops; integrate with GH checks and add 'security-approve' label requirement for high-risk diffs
Build daily drift detection job (Cloud Scheduler/GHA) and console alerting; integrate with existing telemetry and PagerDuty runbooks
Author upgrade playbook with canary strategy: staged account rollouts, timing windows, health checks, and rollback criteria
Write acceptance/integration tests that run the module against a disposable account and assert service entitlements remain intact
Create dashboards showing binding churn, number of high-risk diffs, failed drift checks, and mean time to rollback
Coordinate with Solutions Engineering for two pilot customers and schedule runbook walkthroughs
notes: Trade-offs considered: strong enforcement in CI reduces risk but increases friction for urgent patches. We will add an emergency bypass process with audit and postmortem requirements.
We evaluated an automated policy-rewrite tool but rejected for now due to high false-positive rate on cross-account principals.
Prefer emitting an ordered 'delta-sequence' JSON rather than relying on Terraform module internals to control apply order so external orchestration (Argo/Spinnaker) can sequence applies consistently.

Plan scanner will classify diff types: add-safe, add-risky (new wide-binding), modify-safe (tighten), modify-risky (widen), remove-risky. Only modify-risky and remove-risky require explicit security approval.
Module will support an 'ephemeral_session' pattern for developer/service-assumed roles to reduce long-lived high-priv credentials.
We will include a small library of policy snippets (least-priv-action lists) for common Redwood-managed services to prevent ad-hoc wildcard grants.
prs: GH-1256: drift-detector job and pagerduty integration
